Cada filtro de este tema tiene detrás un: Every filter in this topic has an industry behind it. The developing adjustments and the colour matrices are those of any photo app and those of the cinema's colour-grading suite. Convolution is the basic operation of medical image processing and of the systems that read number plates or text, where edges are looked for before anything is recognised, and it gives its name to convolutional neural networks, whose first layers learn kernels very like Sobel's on their own. And the halftone is still how everything with photographs on paper is printed.

What comes next is the applied case of [[av-convolucion|convolution]], with the kernel sliding over a photograph instead of over a signal. The idea is that of the [[cib-filtrado|moving average]], which smoothed a signal by averaging its last values, taken to two dimensions: each pixel is replaced by a weighted sum of its neighbours. The weights are written in a little 3 × 3 table, the kernel, and the operation is called convolution.

La primera fotografía impresa con semito: The first photograph printed with a halftone in a newspaper appeared in New York's Daily Graphic in 1880, and for a century the screen was made with glass grids in front of the film. The Sobel operator was presented by Irwin Sobel and Gary Feldman in 1968, at Stanford's artificial intelligence laboratory, as a cheap way of estimating an image's gradient. And when Instagram came out in 2010 with a dozen single-pixel filters, almost all of them imitated the colour defects of cheap films and cameras of the 1970s.
